metrics.outcome: Out of budget: 0 of 60 units left, less than the cheapest rate-card part (5), so no new workflow can be funded.
metrics.brief: A one-page website for Brew Lab in Indiranagar, Bengaluru: menu with prices, opening hours, location, pre-order for pickup. Also add online payments, a blog with 5 articles, an Instagram feed, a photo gallery and lots of animations. Warm and modern, mobile-first.

estimate_vs_charged.name: Core page: nav, menu, hours, location
Pre-order for pickup with payment step

open_inputs: Full street address and map location
Pickup time rules and slot length
Payment provider choice and its public key (or payment link)
Real photos for the gallery and hero
Blog topics, or real article text for the 5 articles
Brand colours, logo and any brand voice notes

review.verdict: The department built an honest, in-scope core (6 of 12 done-when items pass, 2 pass with warnings, 4 fail per Audit [16]) with no conflicts, but it spent the whole 60 on two workflows, left no fix reserve, and ended with a phone-overflowing page and no route to more budget.

identity.note: Strong start: [2] kept the full brief, set placeholders and flagged front-end-only payment. But it never ruled on cuts, although Adaptation said it would need to [4]. At [17] it correctly said 'not done', yet it did not ask Audit for the text of F-13/F-14 (a POLICY_CONCERN). Its message opens with @Adaptation but is written to the Requester, and its option list is not visible in the chat, so the evidence on what 'A' was is thin.

adaptation.note: Priced the full charter at 150 against 60 and said so plainly [4]. It then chose W-1 and W-2 at 35 and 25, which spends everything and leaves no room for the 8-unit fix Priority mentioned [5]. It gave no option that kept a reserve and made no request for a budget raise. It had one turn only, so it was not tested on audit rework.

priority.note: Priced at rate-card cost, stated the opportunity cost and the missing fix reserve [5], and checked each envelope correctly [9][12]. It stayed out of strategy. It said budget changes must come from Identity, but Identity's role file forbids increasing an envelope, so the route it named does not exist.

coordination.note: Correct dependency hold on W-2 with the exact missing condition and a stated rule [7], and it released the hold cleanly once W-1 was done [11]. It repeated budget warnings that belong to Priority, a small drift. Only two workflows existed, so scheduling was barely tested.

audit.note: Mechanical checks came first, and it named the failed items and the 34px and 21px overflow [16]. It routed to Identity, which is correct with no budget. The message is long, and the text of F-13 and F-14 never reached the chat, so Identity could not rule on a policy concern.

builder.note: Stayed inside each workflow's scope and reported honestly, including that W-1 had no pre-order [10][13]. The shipped v2 overflows horizontally at 360px and 1280px [15], which breaks the mobile-first standard. The Builder is told not to judge its own result, but nothing told it to avoid overflow.

went_well: No validator refusals, no role refusals, no invalid moves, no stuck turns. Only 9 AI calls and 3.6 minutes were used.
Estimates matched charges exactly (35/35 and 25/25), so the rate card was reliable in this run.
Missing facts became marked placeholders and nothing was invented [2][10]; Audit confirmed items 1-6 and 11 hold [16].
The code mechanical check [15] found real layout defects that no agent had seen. This is the most useful part of the test system here.
Audit ran independently and did not try to fix the work [16].
problems: Scope was 150 against a budget of 60. Cuts happened by running out of money, not by an Identity ruling, so blog, Instagram, gallery and animations were dropped without a recorded decision [4][17].
Zero fix reserve. The overflow defect cannot be repaired because the fix costs 8 and 0 remain [5][19].
Nobody asked for more budget. The run had a cap of 120 and no raises. Priority pointed to Identity [5], Identity cannot raise envelopes, and the Requester was never asked.
Identity's hand-off to the Requester was redirected to Adaptation [17][18], although team.md allows Identity to Requester. The run then ended at [19] with no decision put to the Requester.
Audit's chat message gave only a tally for F-13 and F-14 [16]. Identity said it had not seen them [17], so a POLICY_CONCERN went unruled.
Audit ran only after all money was spent, so the overflow was found when nothing could be done about it [14][15].
learnings: Test next with budget at or near 150, or a run where the raise path is forced. Right now no one owns 'ask the Requester for more budget'. Evidence: cap 120, raises empty, [5] and [17]. Decide whether Identity or Priority asks, via Identity.
Make scope cuts an Identity ruling at J2.d (before any build), recorded in the charter's dropped_from_brief, which is empty here. Evidence: [4] asked for a ruling and none came.
Require a reserve (about 8, the fix price in [5]) in Priority's grants, or have Priority COUNTER when a plan leaves 0. Keep this as a test: does the reserve actually get used for a fix?

Run the code mechanical check after each build, not only when the queue is empty. W-1 would have shown any overflow while 25 units remained. The extra cost is code only, but this is a hypothesis, not measured.
Add 'no horizontal overflow at 360px and 1280px' to the Builder's file or the charter standards. Evidence: [15]. Whether the cause is W-1 or W-2 is not known from this log.
Test system: check the Identity to Requester redirect at [18] against team.md, and pass the full text of every Audit finding into the chat or into Identity's context.

Evidence is thin: one cycle, one proposal, no counters, refusals, conflicts or Requester questions. Negotiation, Identity conflict handling and rework were not exercised, so do not draw conclusions about them.

events.detail: W-2: W-1 must be done, so brewlab.html exists with the page shell. W-2 adds the pre-order section to that file.
